## T3.3 Complete — Regression & Crossover Estimation

### OLS Log-linear Regression: **Δ = −12.00 + 0.530 · log₂(N)**

| Statistic | Value |
|-----------|-------|
| Intercept *a* | −11.9996 |
| Slope *b* | +0.5305 |
| R² | **0.6130** |
| p-value (slope) | 0.0374 ✓ significant |
| 95% CI (slope) | [0.046, 1.015] |

### Crossover N\*

| Item | Value | Note |
|------|-------|------|
| Point estimate N\* | **6,448,676** | 2^(−a/b) |
| Bootstrap 95% CI | [40,325 — 1,000,000,000] | Very wide; right tail hits clip at 1e9 |
| Flag | `extrapolated_above_range` | N\* >> tested max of 60,000 |
| R² flag | None — R² = 0.613 ≥ 0.5 | |

### Key Interpretive Findings

1. **All 7 Δ values are negative** — data augmentation *hurts* accuracy at 5-epoch training across every tested size. This is the well-known under-training effect: augmentation increases effective variance when the model hasn't converged.
2. **Positive slope b = +0.530** confirms the trend is monotonically improving: augmentation becomes progressively *less harmful* as training set size grows.
3. **N\* ≈ 6.45 million** is far beyond the tested range (500–60,000), meaning augmentation would not break even within the studied regime. The bootstrap CI is very wide (40K → 1B), reflecting high uncertainty in extrapolation.
4. **R² = 0.613** — the log-linear model explains ~61% of variance; fit is moderate but statistically significant (p = 0.037).

### Artifacts produced
- **`analysis/regression_results.json`** — OLS coefficients (a, b, R², p-value, slope CI), N\* point estimate, bootstrap 95% CI, and interpretive flags
- **`analysis/bootstrap_N_star.csv`** — exactly 5,000 rows (`iter`, `N_star_boot`) of the bootstrap N\* distribution
